summary: The word "هَلُمَّ" (halumma) means "come." It can be used intransitively, like "come to us," or transitively, like "bring your witnesses." It's a versatile command to approach or bring something.
lane: هَلُمَّ ذ i. q. نَعَالَ Come. (S, K, &c.) -b2- It is intrans.; as in هَلُمَّ إِلَيْنَا Come to us. And tran also; as in هَلُمَّ شُهَدَآءَ كُمْ Cause your witnesses to come; bring your witnesses. (Msb.) -b3- هَلُمَّ جَرًّا At thine ease: see 1 in art. جر .
